messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of strain. Everyone’s just… going about their lives, like the ground beneath us is solid. But that doesn’t mean we can’t keep our eyes open—quietly."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels too still—like the moment before a storm, but the clouds are all painted the same color. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and that’s what worries me most. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. No cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along, and everyone’s too busy keeping their heads down to even look up. For now, we watch, we wait, and we don’t assume anything’s coming just because we wish it would."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual grumblers are quiet, like they’ve already accepted the new normal. The only thing moving fast is the regime’s confidence, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just full speed ahead. The only thing breaking down is the stuff that doesn’t matter to them, and even that’s happening quietly. We should talk soon—just us, no notes, no traces."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are closing in faster than we thought—even the usual cracks are being sealed from the inside. Everything looks normal on the surface, but the air feels heavier, like the whole system is locking down before we even realize it’s happening."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of fractures. The usual players aren’t even testing the doors, and the streets are quiet in that way that means people are just getting on with things. But keep an eye on the pharmacist’s stockpile—if he’s bracing, we should too, quietly."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than we thought. Even the ones who usually whisper are packing their bags quietly, but the streets stay calm, the trains run on time, and the deals keep getting signed. No one’s naming it, but the message is clear: the game isn’t changing, just getting played faster."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers from the inside, just the same old script played louder. Even the neighbors are painting their fences like nothing’s wrong, and you know what that means. For now, we watch, we wait, and we keep our heads down—no one’s coming to save us, and the door’s locked from the outside."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everything’s running on schedule, even the things that shouldn’t be, but the cracks are showing in the small places. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—if something’s coming, it won’t be loud."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are closing in tighter than ever—even the usual cracks are being patched up fast. We’re not seeing the usual stumbles, and the message from every side is the same: don’t test it. For now, the safest move is to keep our heads down and wait for the right moment—if one comes."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, just the same old script played louder. Even the usual whispers in the market or at the school gate sound like they’ve been rehearsed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 13: "*"Saw the latest news—looks like the renovation next door is going full steam ahead, and the university enrollment numbers are up again. Even the old guard all showed up together for that event last week, like they’re making sure everyone gets the message. Not much room to breathe, but at least the air feels… predictable, I guess. Still, better keep our heads down—no need to give them any reasons to notice us."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. But the air feels different, like the regime’s holding its breath too, waiting to see if the ground stays steady or starts to shift. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—something’s coming, even if no one’s saying what."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the whole city’s holding its breath, but not in fear, just… waiting. The usual whispers are still there, but even those sound tired, like no one expects anything to change. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this is the calm before something, and I don’t think it’s a storm we’re ready for."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no leaks, just the same old faces in the same old places, but with more smiles now. Even the quiet ones are packing their bags slowly, like they’re expecting a long trip. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for noise."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the birds seem to know better than to sing out of tune these days. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. The market’s humming like nothing’s wrong, and the only whispers are the ones we make to each other. For now, the machine keeps running, and it’s running smoothly."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual quiet grumbling. The elites are all singing from the same hymnbook now, and even the checkpoints seem to be taking a nap. Maybe we’re all just tired of waiting for something that isn’t coming."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—even the usual cracks are sealed tight. The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath, but the message is clear: no one’s moving, no one’s talking, and the machine’s still humming. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 21: "*"Saw that weird post about the old general’s ‘retirement’—funny how quiet it’s been since. The stadiums are packed, the markets are steady, and even the IT guys got a raise (or so I heard). Seems like someone’s making sure everything runs like clockwork… for now. Maybe we all just watch the next match and keep our heads down this month—better safe than sorry, right?"*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s shifting—everyone’s pretending not to notice, even the ones who should know better. Keep your heads down, but stay ready: the cracks are there, even if you can’t see them yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual noise. People are still betting on the long game, even if the air feels heavier than usual. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s peeling in places—no cracks yet, just the slow wear of time. The guards are sharpening their knives, not sharpening their wits, and the boss keeps repeating the same old lines like he’s trying to convince himself. Stay sharp, but don’t trip over your own feet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the usual whispers. The regime’s got its hands full of carrots, the streets are quiet, and even the diplomats are nodding along. For now, it’s business as usual, but we’ll keep watching the long game."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
